tracks.legalName: Summary Court Expungement of a Non-Conviction, S.C. Code § 17-22-950
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina magistrate or municipal court charge that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-22-950 splits on a single fact: whether the accused person was fingerprinted. Under subsection (A), where charges were brought in a summary court, the person was found not guilty or the charges were dismissed or nolle prossed, and the person WAS fingerprinted, the summary court shall immediately issue an expungement order at no cost, obtain and verify all necessary signatures and distribute copies to the arresting agency, the detention facility, the solicitor's office, the clerk of court where applicable, the summary courts involved and SLED. Nothing is submitted by the participant on that branch. Under subsection (B), where the person was NOT fingerprinted, the accused person may apply to the summary court, at no cost, for an order to expunge, and on application and verification the court shall issue the order and distribute copies to the arresting agency and the summary courts involved but not to SLED. That application is SCCA 223E, a participant-signed form. Both branches are barred where the dismissal occurred at a preliminary hearing or where the person has charges pending in summary court and General Sessions arising out of the same course of events. Subsection (C) fixes the timing at no sooner than the appeal expiration date and no later than thirty days after it. Subsection (E) requires removal from all internet-based public records no later than thirty days from the disposition date regardless of whether an application is made. Subsection (F) allows a prosecution or law enforcement agency to object, on the sole grounds of other pending charges or ineligibility, with written notice to the accused person no later than thirty days after the disposition, in which case a General Sessions judge decides; the objection is transmitted on SCCA 223D1, which is completed by the summary court judge and not by the participant.

exclusions: A dismissal that occurred at a preliminary hearing.
Any case where the person has charges pending in summary court and in a court of general sessions arising out of the same course of events.
Convictions of any kind. This route reaches non-convictions only.

Charges dismissed or nolle prossed because of successful completion of pretrial intervention, the traffic education programme, the alcohol education programme, a conditional discharge or any other statutorily authorised diversion programme operated by a solicitor's office. SCCA 223E says in terms that those must be applied for at the solicitor's office, and they route to their own tracks.
General Sessions charges, which route to sc_17_1_40_general_sessions.

units.label: Fingerprinted: the summary court must issue the order itself, § 17-22-950(A)
units.description: Where the person was fingerprinted for the charge, the summary court shall immediately issue the expungement order at no cost to the accused person, obtain and verify all necessary signatures, and distribute copies to the arresting law enforcement agency, the detention facility or jail, the solicitor's office, the clerk of court in appealed or remanded cases, the summary courts involved and SLED. There is no participant submission on this branch and no fee, so the deliverable is guidance: confirm the disposition date and the appeal expiration date, expect the order within thirty days of the appeal expiration date, obtain the certified or raised-seal copy the court must provide under subsection (D), confirm the charge has come off internet-based public records within thirty days of disposition under subsection (E), and escalate to the summary court clerk where the order did not issue. legalDesignDecision.rationale: The controlling review classified this whole track as process_guidance on the ground that the court issues the order automatically. Read at source, § 17-22-950 does not have one branch but two, and they are selected by a single participant fact. Subsection (A), the fingerprinted branch, is genuinely automatic and court-initiated with nothing for the participant to submit, so guidance is the right output there and the guidance rule expressly permits it. Subsection (B), the unfingerprinted branch, gives the accused person an application to make, and SCCA 223E is that application: an Office of Court Administration form provided under subsection (G), signed by the defendant, every field of which is a participant-supplied fact. A participant-facing application that can be generated from participant answers must be packet-capable, so treating the whole track as guidance would have withheld a free, generable form from exactly the people who need it. The two branches have different initiating actors and different required submissions, exactly one applies, and neither is a step toward the other, so the route is an alternative composition with two units rather than one strategy. Both branches remain free and the review's instruction never to charge for this route is preserved. SCCA 223D1 is not a participant instrument: it is completed by the summary court judge and is recorded as an official source, not as a component.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-1-40(B)(1) provides that where a person's record is expunged under Article 9 of Chapter 22 because the person was charged with a criminal offence, or issued a courtesy summons, and the charge was discharged, proceedings were dismissed, or the person was found not guilty, the arrest and booking record, associated bench warrants, mug shots and fingerprints must be destroyed and no evidence of the record may be retained by any municipal, county or state agency. Two provisos qualify that destruction and must be disclosed: law enforcement and prosecution agencies retain the arrest and booking record, bench warrants, mug shots and fingerprints under seal for three years and one hundred twenty days, and may retain them indefinitely under seal for ongoing or future investigation and prosecution of the offence, administrative hearings and litigation defence; and detention and correctional facilities retain booking records and institutional files under seal for the same period. The route runs through the Solicitor's Office. Section 17-22-940(A)(1) exempts a § 17-1-40 applicant from the $250 administrative fee unless the charge was dismissed, discharged or nolle prossed as part of the plea arrangement under which the defendant pled guilty and was sentenced to other charges; § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts the route from the $25 SLED verification fee and § 17-22-940(E) from SLED verification itself; and § 17-22-940(H) bars the clerk from charging a filing fee where the charge was discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or the applicant was acquitted. Section 17-22-940(G) permits multiple charges from a single incident on one application.

exclusions: Convictions of any kind.
Summary court non-convictions, which are free and route to sc_17_22_950_summary.
Charges dismissed on completion of a diversion programme, which route to their own solicitor tracks.

The sealed retentions the section preserves: law enforcement, prosecution, detention and correctional agencies keep the record under seal for three years and one hundred twenty days, and law enforcement and prosecution may keep it indefinitely under seal for the statutory purposes.
Unredacted incident and supplemental reports, investigative files and gathered evidence, which § 17-1-40(C)(1) preserves under seal.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 17-1-40 imposes no waiting period; the application may be made once the charge is discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or the person is acquitted.

geography.venue: Statewide statute administered circuit by circuit. Apply to the Solicitor's Office in the judicial circuit where the offence was committed; the order is signed by a circuit court judge and filed with the clerk of court.

destination.name: Solicitor's Office in the judicial circuit where the offence was committed
destination.detail: The applicant applies to the solicitor's office, which supplies the mandatory blank order form, assists in completing it, obtains the signatures, files the completed order with the clerk of court and distributes certified copies. No SLED verification is required on this route and no SLED fee is charged.

components.notes: Applicant's expungement application package for the § 17-1-40 General Sessions non-conviction route, generated from the participant's answers and carrying every item the solicitor's office needs to complete the mandatory order form: identity and alias set, SID, county and court of disposition, warrant or indictment numbers, arrest and charge dates, original and final charge, disposition and disposition date, conviction and sentence-completion dates where applicable, and the statutory lane and eligibility recitals for S.C. Code § 17-1-40. It is not a substitute for the official order form. Section 17-22-930 requires the applicant to obtain the blank expungement order form from the solicitor's office in the judicial circuit where the charge originated and makes the use of that form mandatory and to the exclusion of all other expungement forms, so the package is prepared to be transcribed onto the official form with the solicitor's assistance, which section 17-22-940(B)(1) makes that office's duty.

The mandatory order instrument is SCCA 223A1 GS (Revised 04/2026), Order for Destruction of Arrest Records, seven pages, read at source 2026-08-06. It is an order signed by the solicitor and then a circuit court judge, not a participant filing, and the blank is obtained from the solicitor's office under § 17-22-930. The packet identifies it and tells the participant what to ask for.

Checklist naming the SLED criminal history record, the docket from the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court, and a certified disposition where available, with who issues each and what it costs. LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any of them, and none of them delays generation of the package.

Fee schedule and payment instructions for this route: no solicitor administrative fee unless the charge was dismissed, discharged or nolle prossed as part of a plea arrangement under which you pled guilty and were sentenced on other charges; no SLED verification fee; and no clerk of court filing fee where the charge was discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or you were acquitted. Where several charges arose from one incident they may go on one application. All amounts payable by separate certified checks or money orders; personal checks are not accepted, and a single combined instrument is a common cause of rejection.

Instructions covering the application to the Solicitor's Office in the circuit where the offence was committed; that SLED verifies and documents statutory eligibility before anyone signs where verification is required; that the solicitor or designee signs and then a circuit court judge signs; that the solicitor files the completed order with the clerk of court and distributes certified copies; that under § 17-22-940(E)(3) no official may allow the applicant to take possession of the application during the process; that under § 17-22-940(G) each order may contain only one charge except for multiple charges from a single incident under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a); and a post-order verification step against a fresh SLED record.

rules.fees: No $250 solicitor administrative fee, unless the charge was dismissed, discharged or nolle prossed as part of the plea arrangement under which the defendant pled guilty and was sentenced to other charges, in which case the $250 applies. No $25 SLED verification fee. No $35 clerk of court filing fee where the charge was discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or the applicant was acquitted.
rules.feeWaiver: The § 17-22-940(A)(1) exemption is the operative relief on this route and is automatic rather than discretionary. unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether LegalEase may pre-fill the published official order form for the § 17-1-40 General Sessions non-conviction route rather than generating an application package for transcription. Section 17-22-930 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that a person applying to expunge a criminal record 'shall obtain the appropriate blank expungement order form from the solicitor's office in the judicial circuit where the charge originated' and that 'the use of this form is mandatory and to the exclusion of all other expungement forms'. Section 17-22-940(B)(1) makes assisting the applicant in completing the form the solicitor's office's own duty, and § 17-22-940(E)(3) forbids any official allowing the applicant to take possession of the application during the process. controllingAuthority.summary: After successful completion of a pretrial intervention programme the solicitor effects a noncriminal disposition of the charge and the person may apply to have the official record of arrest destroyed. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-22-940(D) requires the circuit pretrial intervention director to attest by signature on the application to the eligibility of the charge for expungement before either the solicitor or his designee and then the circuit court judge signs; § 17-22-940(E) exempts the route from SLED verification and § 17-22-940(E)(1) from the $25 SLED verification fee; and § 17-22-940(G) permits multiple charges from a single incident to be combined on one application, this being one of only two routes for which that is allowed. The pretrial intervention application and participation fees under § 17-22-110 are programme costs, not expungement costs.

exclusions: Any participant who did not successfully complete the programme; violation resumes prosecution.
Convictions of any kind.
Charges never accepted into pretrial intervention, which route by their own disposition.
The sealed retentions preserved by § 17-1-40.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond successful completion of the programme and the solicitor's noncriminal disposition.

components.notes: Applicant's expungement application package for the § 17-22-150(a) pretrial intervention route, generated from the participant's answers and carrying every item the solicitor's office needs to complete the mandatory order form: identity and alias set, SID, county and court of disposition, warrant or indictment numbers, arrest and charge dates, original and final charge, disposition and disposition date, conviction and sentence-completion dates where applicable, and the statutory lane and eligibility recitals for S.C. Code § 17-22-150(a). It is not a substitute for the official order form. Section 17-22-930 requires the applicant to obtain the blank expungement order form from the solicitor's office in the judicial circuit where the charge originated and makes the use of that form mandatory and to the exclusion of all other expungement forms, so the package is prepared to be transcribed onto the official form with the solicitor's assistance, which section 17-22-940(B)(1) makes that office's duty.

The mandatory order instrument is SCCA 223A1 GS (Revised 04/2026), Order for Destruction of Arrest Records, seven pages, read at source 2026-08-06. It is an order signed by the solicitor and then a circuit court judge, not a participant filing, and the blank is obtained from the solicitor's office under § 17-22-930. The packet identifies it and tells the participant what to ask for.

Neutral request correspondence the participant sends to the Circuit Pretrial Intervention Director for the circuit that administered the programme, asking them to attest by signature on the application to the eligibility of the charge for expungement, as § 17-22-940(D) requires before either the solicitor or his designee and then the circuit court judge signs. LegalEase drafts the request and names the recipient; the attestation itself is the third party's and is left blank.

Checklist naming the SLED criminal history record, the docket from the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court, and a certified disposition where available, with who issues each and what it costs. LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any of them, and none of them delays generation of the package.

Fee schedule and payment instructions for this route: $250 solicitor administrative fee per order; no SLED verification fee, because § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts this route; and the $35 clerk of court filing fee. Where several charges arose from one incident they may go on one application under § 17-22-940(G). All amounts payable by separate certified checks or money orders; personal checks are not accepted, and a single combined instrument is a common cause of rejection.

Instructions covering the application to the Solicitor's Office in the circuit where the offence was committed; that SLED verifies and documents statutory eligibility before anyone signs where verification is required; that the solicitor or designee signs and then a circuit court judge signs; that the solicitor files the completed order with the clerk of court and distributes certified copies; that under § 17-22-940(E)(3) no official may allow the applicant to take possession of the application during the process; that under § 17-22-940(G) each order may contain only one charge except for multiple charges from a single incident under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a); and a post-order verification step against a fresh SLED record.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records After Successful Alcohol Education Program Completion, S.C. Code § 17-22-530(A)
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina underage-alcohol charge after you completed the Alcohol Education Program

controllingAuthority.summary: The controlling citation is settled at source. Article 5 of Chapter 22, Title 17 is the Alcohol Education Program: § 17-22-510 gives each circuit solicitor prosecutorial discretion to establish the programme, § 17-22-520 sets eligibility, and § 17-22-530 governs disposition on completion. Under § 17-22-530(A), when a person successfully completes an alcohol education programme the circuit solicitor shall effect a noncriminal disposition of the alcohol-related offence and no record may be maintained except by the Commission on Prosecution Coordination to prevent a second use; under § 17-22-530(B) the person may then apply to the court for an order to destroy all official records relating to the arrest. Section 17-22-520 confines eligibility to a person at least seventeen but under twenty-one at the time of arrest, with no prior alcohol-related offence and no significant history of prior delinquency or criminal activity, charged with one of eleven enumerated offences or another offence similar in nature and severity as determined by the circuit solicitor, expressly excluding the offences enumerated in §§ 56-5-2930 and 56-5-2933. Participation is once only. Section 17-22-940(D) names the alcohol education program director as an attestor and § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts § 17-22-530(A) from the SLED verification fee.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 44-53-450(A) allows a person not previously convicted of any offence under Article 3 of Chapter 53, Title 44, or under any state or federal marijuana, stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drug statute, who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession of a controlled substance under § 44-53-370(c) or (d) or § 44-53-375(A), to be placed on probation without entry of a judgment of guilt, with the court discharging the person and dismissing the proceedings on fulfilment of the terms. The discharge is not a conviction for purposes of any disqualification or disability, a nonpublic record is retained by the Department of Narcotic and Dangerous Drugs under SLED solely to determine whether a later offence is a subsequent one, and the discharge and dismissal may occur only once with respect to any person. Subsection (B) is the expungement: on dismissal and discharge the person may apply to the court for an order expunging from all official records, other than the retained nonpublic record, all recordation relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and the dismissal and discharge, and if the court determines after hearing that the person was dismissed and discharged it shall enter the order, restoring the person in the contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest. Subsection (C) requires payment before discharge of a fee of $350 in general sessions court or $150 in summary court, waivable, reducible or suspendable only for indigency. controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 22-5-910(A) allows a defendant convicted of a crime carrying a penalty of not more than thirty days imprisonment or a one thousand dollar fine, or both, or a first offence for unlawful possession of a firearm or weapon carrying not more than one year or a one thousand dollar fine, or both, to apply after three years from the date of the conviction to the circuit court for an order expunging the records of the arrest and conviction and any associated bench warrant; the section does not apply to an offence involving the operation of a motor vehicle. Subsection (B) sets five years for a domestic violence third degree conviction under § 16-25-20(D), or § 16-25-20(B)(1) as it existed before June 4, 2015. Subsection (C) requires no other conviction, including out-of-state convictions, during the applicable period. Subsection (E) defines conviction to include a guilty plea, a plea of nolo contendere or the forfeiting of bail, and provides that any number of subsection (A) offences sentenced at a single sentencing proceeding that are closely connected and arose out of the same incident may be treated as one conviction for expungement purposes. Subsection (F) bars expungement where the person has pending criminal charges of any kind unless they have been pending more than five years, tolled for any time under a bench warrant for failure to appear, allows the relief once only, and applies retroactively. controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 22-5-920(B)(1) allows a defendant with a first offence conviction as a youthful offender, for which the defendant was sentenced pursuant to Chapter 19 of Title 24, the Youthful Offender Act, and who has not been convicted of any offence including an out-of-state offence while serving the youthful offender sentence including probation and parole and for a period of five years from the date of completion of that sentence, to apply to the circuit court for an order expunging the records of the arrest and conviction. Convictions for driving under suspension, and for disturbing schools under § 16-17-420 before May 17, 2018, are excepted from the disqualifying set. Subsection (B)(2) excludes an offence involving the operation of a motor vehicle, an offence classified as a violent crime in § 16-1-60, an offence contained in Chapter 25 of Title 16 except as otherwise provided in § 16-25-30, and an offence for which registration is required under the Sex Offender Registry Act. Subsection (B)(3) makes the relief once only and applies it retroactively. Subsection (A) defines conviction to include a guilty plea, a plea of nolo contendere or the forfeiting of bail, and allows any number of offences receiving a youthful offender sentence at a single sentencing proceeding that are closely connected and arose out of the same incident to be treated as one conviction for expungement purposes. Section 17-22-940(E) requires SLED verification with the $25 fee and provides that a minor traffic-related conviction unrelated to driving under the influence is not a bar.

exclusions: Any person who was merely eligible for a Youthful Offender Act sentence but was not actually sentenced under Chapter 19 of Title 24.
Any offence involving the operation of a motor vehicle, § 22-5-920(B)(2)(a).
Any offence classified as a violent crime in § 16-1-60, § 22-5-920(B)(2)(b).
Any offence contained in Chapter 25 of Title 16, except as otherwise provided in § 16-25-30, § 22-5-920(B)(2)(c).
Any offence for which registration is required under the South Carolina Sex Offender Registry Act, § 22-5-920(B)(2)(d).

Any person convicted of any offence, including an out-of-state offence, while serving the youthful offender sentence or during the five years following its completion, other than a conviction for driving under suspension or for disturbing schools under § 16-17-420 before May 17, 2018.
Any person who has already used the section once.

waitingPeriods.duration: Five years from the date of completion of the sentence, including probation and parole, with no disqualifying conviction either during service of the sentence or during those five years.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read in full at source on 2026-08-06, § 22-5-930 has two branches. Subsection (A) reaches a first offence conviction for either simple possession of a controlled substance under Article 3 of Chapter 53, Title 44, or unlawful possession of a prescription drug under § 40-43-86(EE), including charges for which the person would now be eligible for a conditional discharge under § 44-53-450, and allows application to the circuit court three years from the date of completion of the sentence including probation and parole, whether the conviction was in magistrates or general sessions court. Subsection (B) reaches a first offence conviction for possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance under the same article and allows application twenty years from the date of completion of any sentence including probation and parole for a drug conviction or any felony conviction. Subsection (C) requires no other conviction, including out-of-state convictions, during the three-year period, or no other drug or felony conviction during the twenty-year period. Subsection (D) bars expungement while criminal charges of any kind are pending unless they have been pending more than five years, tolled for time under a bench warrant for failure to appear; allows the relief once only; and bars it where the person has had a conditional discharge within the five years before the arrest for a simple possession of marijuana charge, or within the ten years before the arrest for any other controlled substance or a prescription drug charge. The section applies retroactively but does not affect a pre-existing enhanced conviction or sentence. Subsection (E) requires SLED to keep a nonpublic record.

exclusions: Any drug conviction that is not a first offence within the meaning of the subsection relied on.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Expunge an Old Unlawful Handgun Possession Conviction, S.C. Code § 17-1-65
tracks.publicName: Clear an old South Carolina unlawful handgun possession conviction — the window closes 7 March 2029

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-1-65 provides that a person may apply for an expungement of one conviction for unlawful possession of a handgun as provided in § 16-23-20, if the conviction occurred prior to the enactment of the South Carolina Constitutional Carry/Second Amendment Preservation Act of 2024, and that an application under the section must be made within five years of the enactment of the section. The section was created by 2024 Act No. 111 (H.3594), § 20, effective March 7, 2024, which fixes both dates: the conviction must predate March 7, 2024, and the application must be made before March 7, 2029. SCCA 223C (06/2024), read at source on the same date, is the instrument for this route and not a general-purpose General Sessions destruction order: it recites that the defendant is entitled to have the records expunged 'according to S.C. Code Ann. § 17-1-65' and carries three findings tracking the section exactly — conviction under § 16-23-20 prior to the enactment of the Act on March 7, 2024; application submitted prior to March 7, 2029; and no previous application for expungement of a handgun possession conviction under § 17-1-65. The form also recites the § 17-1-40 sealed retentions and the § 22-5-910 SLED nonpublic retention, so the surviving records are stated on the order itself. This is a closing window and the deadline should be surfaced unprompted.

exclusions: Any conviction for unlawful possession of a handgun occurring on or after March 7, 2024, the date the Constitutional Carry/Second Amendment Preservation Act of 2024 was enacted.
Any conviction under a provision other than § 16-23-20.
More than one conviction; the section reaches one conviction only.
Any person who has previously applied for expungement of a handgun possession conviction under § 17-1-65.
Any application made on or after March 7, 2029, when the five-year window closes permanently.
The sealed and nonpublic retentions the SCCA 223C order itself recites under §§ 17-1-40 and 22-5-910.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 17-1-65 imposes no waiting period. It imposes a deadline instead: the application must be made within five years of the section's enactment, that is before March 7, 2029.
